newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end up on ratio cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end up on ratio cut hopes.

text.p: China's A and B share indices closed up on Friday due to strong rumours that China will soon cut bank reserve ratios, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index rose 0.899 points or 1.48 percent to 61.678 points, while Shenzhen's B share index edged up 1.27 points or 0.90 percent to close at 142.00 points.
Brokers in both Shanghai and Shenzhen said rumours the suggested the central bank could announce a cut in bank reserve ratios as early as this weekend.

Despite the rises, market sentiment remained cautious due to concerns that the authorities could unveil specific measures to implement a ban on domestic investors buying B shares during a national meeting of bankers next week, brokers said.

"Buying was sporadic with major investors cautious on the concerns," one Shanghai broker said. "They are worried that (measures to ban domestic investors from B shares) will cause the market to fall."
"Institutions largely adopted a wait-and-see attitude towards trading ahead of the weekend," a Shenzhen broker said. "It remains unclear as to whether the upward trend can extend into next week."
In Shanghai's B share market, newcomer clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was still the most active stock on institutional support, rising 2.53 percent to $0.324 on volume of 5.9 million shares.

In Shenzhen, Changan Automobile B share was the most active on volume of 1.39 million shares, adding HK$0.03 to HK$4.51. Appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the biggest B share gainer, rising 3.03 percent to HK$3.74.

The A share indices in Shanghai and Shenzhen rose, with Shanghai's A index up 11.871 points or 1.25 percent to 958.913 points and Shenzhen's A index rising 3.62 points or 1.08 percent to end at 337.24.

In Shanghai, Xinjiang Tunhe A share was the biggest winner on news that it had bought shares in a trust and investment firm, soaring 1.23 yuan or limit-up of 10 percent to 13.48 yuan on volume of 2.8 million shares.
In Shenzhen, Kunming Department Store A share, which owns a share of a private bank, closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 6.99 yuan on heavy volume of 11.07 million shares.
